newsitem.title: QATAR: Bahrain may skip GCC meeting ahead of summit.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain may skip GCC meeting ahead of summit.

text.p: Bahrain is unlikely to attend a meeting of Gulf Arab foreign ministers due to be held in Qatar on Saturday to prepare for an upcoming summit, a Qatari official said on Wednesday.

The official, however, did not rule out a decision by Bahrain, locked in a territorial dispute with Qatar, to reverse a threat to boycott the summit by leaders of the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) in December.

"Qatar has received confirmation from the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the UAE that they would be attending Saturday's preparatory meeting, but Bahrain has not replied as yet," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
"We think Bahrain will not attend (the meeting) on Saturday, but eventually they will come for the GCC summit next month."
The GCC's annual summit is scheduled to be held in Doha on December 7 to 9.

Last month Bahrain threatened to boycott the summit unless Doha withdrew a lawsuit it has filed at the International Court of Justice at The Hague over a number of barren islands, sandbanks and reefs controlled by Bahrain but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has rejected Bahrain's threat to boycott the summit, saying it would only withdraw the case if Saudi mediation to resolve the dispute succeeded.
